tools.description: Mark one stored event deleted: the same soft delete a NIP-09 request from the author makes. The event leaves REQ and COUNT and keeps its row, so `get_event` and `list_events` still return it with `deleted_at` set — unless an actionable report hides it, in which case it stays hidden until the report is allowed. The argument is the event's hex id; a prefix shorter than 64 characters is refused rather than widened to whatever the store's range would match. Answers `outcome` — `deleted`, `already_deleted`, `not_deleteable` (kind 62 is never deleted), or `not_found` — and the row as it stands after the call

id.description: The event's hex id, in either case; a prefix shorter than 64 characters is refused and deletes nothing

tools.name: delete_event

tools.description: Read one stored event by its exact 64-character hex id, in either case; null when no such id is stored

id.description: The event's 64-character hex id, in either case.

tools.name: get_event

tools.description: Read one invoice by id, whatever its status; `invoice` is null when no row carries the id. The id is the invoice's own opaque identifier — not a 64-character hex id — and is taken verbatim. A confirmed invoice can still read `status: "pending"`: confirmation sets `amount_paid` and `confirmed_at`, and only a status update moves the status

id.description: The invoice's own identifier, taken verbatim — not a hex id

tools.name: invoices_get

tools.description: List the pending invoices, oldest first, paged by `offset` and `limit` — the store's own pending walk, so a completed or expired invoice is not here and `invoices_get` is how to read one whatever its status. `limit` is 1 to 500 rows, absent 500; `offset` skips that many, and at most 5000. A confirmed invoice stays in this list while its status reads `pending`

limit.description: Page size: 1 to 500 rows, oldest first; absent uses 500.

offset.description: Rows to skip, oldest first; absent skips none; at most 5000.

tools.name: invoices_list

tools.description: List stored events matching the given kinds, authors, ids, since and until. Rows come back oldest first, and `limit` is the page size — the first rows in that order, at most 500; `truncated` is true when the page is full, so more rows may match

authors.description:
Author pubkey hex prefixes, 4 to 64 characters each in either case; at most 64 per
call. A criterion the wire would refuse is an error, not a narrower read.

ids.description: Event id hex prefixes, 4 to 64 characters each in either case; at most 64 per call.

kinds.description: Kinds to select; absent selects every kind.

limit.description:
Page size: 1 to 500 rows, and they are the first rows in the payload's order; absent
uses 500, the store's own page.

since.description: Events created at or after this unix second.

until.description: Events created at or before this unix second.

tools.name: list_events

tools.description: Read the last retention purge this process ran: `run` is null until a `maintenance_run` call in this process records one, and otherwise carries `ranAt` and the `deleted`, `expired` and `retained` counts. It reports this door's own runs — the daemon's maintenance worker runs in another process and its passes are not visible here
tools.name: maintenance_last_run

tools.description: Run the retention purge now — the purge step of the maintenance worker's pass, over this process's store. When `limits.event.retention.maxDays` is absent or not positive the purge is skipped: the store is not called and the answer is three zeros. Answers `run` — `ranAt`, and `deleted`, `expired` and `retained` as the store counted them; the same object is what `maintenance_last_run` reports
tools.name: maintenance_run

tools.description: Read the relay's status: the software version, the relay process's uptime, its live connection count and its worker rows, and the NIP-11 document it advertises. Facts only the relay process can know come from the status document it publishes; when that document is absent, unreadable or older than its freshness bound they are null, and `relay.reason` says which
tools.name: relay_status

tools.description: Act on one report event: `hide` marks its targets hidden (`actionable: true`, so REQ and COUNT withhold them while `nip56.hideActionableReports` is on) and `allow` clears them (`actionable: false`). The argument is the report's own kind-1984 event id — exactly 64 hex characters, not the reported event's id — and every report row that event wrote is flipped. Answers `reports` (the rows as they stand, by `id`) and `changed` (how many this call flipped). Every new REQ reflects the change at once; already-connected subscriptions see it at the relay's next refresh, up to 30 s

action.description: `hide` marks the report's targets hidden; `allow` clears them

id.description: The report's own kind-1984 event id, exactly 64 hex characters in either case; not the reported event's id

tools.name: reports_action

tools.description: The review queue: the reports still actionable, newest first, at most `limit` — 1 to 500, absent 500. This is not every report: a report an operator allowed has left the queue, and the queue has no offset, so there is nothing to page. `reports_action` takes the `event_id` this list shows, not the row's own `id`

limit.description: Page size: 1 to 500 reports, newest first; absent uses 500.

tools.name: reports_list

tools.description: Read the merged settings document, narrowed to the defaults' keys and redacted. The document arrives under `settings`
tools.name: settings_get

tools.description: Write settings: one path as {"path": "wot.enabled", "value": false}, or several as {"changes": [{"path": …, "value": …}, …]}. No other keys are accepted
tools.name: settings_set

tools.description: Administer one pubkey's user row: `admit` sets `is_admitted` and stamps `tos_accepted_at` from the server clock, `revoke` clears `is_admitted` and writes no row for a pubkey that has none, and `vanish`/`unvanish` set and clear the stored vanished flag, writing a minimal row (not admitted, balance 0) when the pubkey has none. These are the same writes the relay's own strategies make, with one difference each: `vanish` publishes no kind-62 request and deletes no event, `unvanish` is the only path in the tree that clears the flag, and an admitted pubkey is still held to `limits.event.pubkey.minBalance` by the relay's gate. Answers `action` and the row as it stands after the call — `user` null when no row exists, `balance` 0 for that same pubkey — so `revoke` and an unknown key answer the same shape as `admit`

pubkey.description: The pubkey's 64-character hex key, in either case

tools.name: user_admin

tools.description: Read one pubkey's stored user row — `is_admitted`, `is_vanished`, `balance` in msats and the two timestamps — and its balance on its own, so a missing row and an empty balance are different answers: `user` is null and `balance` is 0 for a pubkey with no row. `is_vanished` is the stored flag, never hydrated from a kind-62 request by this tool, so a pubkey the relay has not cached and the door has never written reads as absent. Changes nothing

pubkey.description: The pubkey's 64-character hex key, in either case

tools.name: user_get
